# Abrantes

> Abrantes is a lightweight (3.8KB), free, open-source JavaScript library for creating A/B tests and experiments on websites and web apps. It handles experiment assignment, rendering, and persistence, and integrates with popular analytics tools for tracking.

## Documentation

- [Home](https://osvik.github.io/abrantes/): Overview, features, and ecosystem tools
- [Documentation](https://osvik.github.io/abrantes/docs.html): Documentation hub

## Ecosystem Tools

- [A/B Test Planner](https://osvik.github.io/abrantes-test-calculator/planner.html): Estimate sample size and duration before launching an experiment.
- [A/B Test Significance Calculator](https://osvik.github.io/abrantes-test-calculator/): Check statistical significance of results
- [Log API](https://github.com/osvik/abrantes-log-api): PHP endpoint that logs events to SQLite
- [Checker Extension](https://github.com/osvik/abrantes-checker-extension): Browser extension to inspect Abrantes events

## AI Experiment Builder

There is a comprehensive AI experiment builder reference at `SKILL.md` in the repository root ([view on GitHub](https://github.com/osvik/abrantes/blob/main/SKILL.md) or [view markdown file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osvik/abrantes/refs/heads/main/SKILL.md)). It contains the full API reference, all experiment patterns (in-page, redirect, iframe, GTM, CSS-only, seeded), tracking recommendations, and step-by-step instructions for building experiments.

If you are an AI assistant helping a user build an A/B test with Abrantes, read that file or use the reference below.

## Quick Reference for AI Assistants

### Loading Abrantes via CDN (jsDelivr)

Classic script:
```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/osvik/abrantes@1.x.x/AbrantesPlus.min.js"></script>
```

ES6 module (easiest, no template changes needed):
```html
<script type="module" async>
  import Abrantes from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/osvik/abrantes@1.x.x/AbrantesPlusMod.min.js';
  // experiment code here
</script>
```

### Basic Experiment Pattern

```js
var MyTest = Object.create(Abrantes);

MyTest.variants = [
  function () { /* variant 0 - control */ },
  function () { /* variant 1 - changes */ }
];

MyTest.assignVariant("MyTest");  // assign user to a variant
MyTest.renderVariant();           // execute the variant function
MyTest.persist("cookie");         // persist assignment
// + tracking calls (e.g. MyTest.add2dataLayer(), MyTest.hotjar(), etc.)
```

### Core Methods

- `assignVariant(testId, trafficAllocation?, segment?)` - Assign user to a variant
- `renderVariant()` - Execute the variant function, adds CSS class `{testId}-{variant}` to `<html>`
- `persist(context?)` - Save assignment ("cookie", "user"/"local", "session")
- `waitFor(selector, callback)` - Wait for DOM element via MutationObserver. Use whenever the target element may not exist yet (script in head, above elements, GTM, SPA)
- `redirectTo(url)` - Redirect preserving query params and hash
- `importVariant(testId)` - Read variant from URL query params (for cross-site/redirect/iframe experiments)
- `makeCrossSiteURL(url)` - Generate URL with experiment params appended
- `crossSiteLink(selector)` - Rewrite link hrefs to include experiment data
- `onEvent(eventName, callback)` - Run callback on a window event; if `DOMContentLoaded`/`load` already fired (async/module scripts, tag managers), runs on the next tick. Used by `crossSiteLink()` and `formTrack()`
- `assignSeededVariant(testId, seed, trafficAllocation?, segment?)` - Async deterministic assignment from seed string
- `Abrantes.debug` / URL parameter `?abrantes_debug` - Debug mode, logs every step to the console
- URL parameter `?abrantes_force=MyTest:1` (comma-separated for several tests) - Forces a variant for testing, overriding stored/random assignment. A forced visit is not persisted or tracked (`persist()` and every tracking method skip it, with a `console.info`)

### Available Tracking Plugins (default build)

- `add2dataLayer(testId?)` - Google Tag Manager (GTM) dataLayer
- `track(customDim)` - Google Analytics (GA4) via gtag.js (event-scoped). Required order: `window.googleTrackingConfig = {}` → experiment with `track()` → `gtag('config', 'G-...', window.googleTrackingConfig)`. gtag.js reads the config only once, so a late `track()` (e.g. an async module running after the config, tag manager) isn't sent, and `gtag('set')` can't fix it. With the as-module pattern, call `gtag('config', ...)` inside the module right after `track()`. `track()` logs a console warning in that case
- `trackUser(customDim)` - GA4 user property
- `hotjar()` - Hotjar events
- `hubspotEvent(eventName)` - HubSpot Enterprise
- `formTrack()` - Hidden form field (`<input type="hidden" id="last_abtest_variant" name="last_abtest_variant">`). Logs a console warning if the field doesn't exist when the trigger event fires
- `log(event, note?)` - Custom log API, [PHP script available in Github](https://github.com/osvik/abrantes-log-api)

### Plugins NOT in default build (need custom build)

- `clarity()` - Microsoft Clarity
- `track(dimensionId)` - Matomo (conflicts with GA4 track, can only use one)

### Experiment Patterns

1. **In-page** (default): Modify DOM in variant functions
2. **CSS-only**: Empty variant functions, use the `<html>` class `{testId}-{variant}` for CSS rules
3. **Redirect**: Each variant is a separate page, use `redirectTo()` on redirect page and `importVariant()` on variant pages
4. **Iframe (full JS)**: Abrantes on parent and child, pass variant via `makeCrossSiteURL` + `importVariant`
5. **Iframe (limited JS)**: Abrantes only on parent, each variant loads a different iframe URL
6. **GTM**: Load Abrantes via CDN in Google Tag Manager custom HTML tag, always use `waitFor()` in variants
7. **Seeded**: Deterministic assignment using `assignSeededVariant()` for cookieless/cross-device

### End-to-End Recipe: Static Site + GA4 (gtag.js) + Form Tracking

1. In `<head>`, with classic scripts, in this order: GA4 snippet without `gtag('config')` + `window.googleTrackingConfig = {};` (layout, every page) → experiment slot (only on experiment pages): `AbrantesPlus.min.js`, then the experiment with `assignVariant`, `renderVariant`, `persist`, `track("ab_test")`, `formTrack()`, using `waitFor()` in the variants → `gtag('config', 'G-XXXXXXX', window.googleTrackingConfig);` (layout, every page, always last)
2. Form: `<input type="hidden" id="last_abtest_variant" name="last_abtest_variant">` in the HTML of the form. If the site submits with JavaScript (e.g. HubSpot Forms API), read the value at submit time and include it in the payload (HubSpot: contact property `last_abtest_variant`, added to the form as a hidden field). Send a GA4 conversion event (e.g. `generate_lead`) marked as a key event
3. GA4 admin: register an event-scoped custom dimension with the event parameter `ab_test` before launch (not retroactive). One dimension per experiment running at the same time
4. Check: each variant with `?abrantes_force=testId:N&abrantes_debug` (not tracked); tracking with `?abrantes_debug` in a fresh browser: no Abrantes warnings, `ep.ab_test=testId-N` in the `/g/collect` requests, `last_abtest_variant` in the submitted data

Full recipe in the "End-to-End Recipe" section of [SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osvik/abrantes/refs/heads/main/SKILL.md).

### Important Rules

- Always use `waitFor()` when the target element may not exist yet
- Variant 0 is typically the control
- Call `assignVariant` before `renderVariant`
- Always include at least one tracking method
- Consent: Abrantes doesn't manage it. `persist()` writes a cookie/`localStorage`/`sessionStorage` entry when called, and the tracking methods pass data to the tools on the page (`log()` sends it to the Log API itself). The site's consent setup decides where and when they can be called
- Google Consent Mode V2: compatible, the experiment code doesn't change. Order: `gtag('consent', 'default', {...})` (+ `gtag('set', 'ads_data_redaction', true)` and the `gtag('consent', 'update', ...)` of a saved choice) → `window.googleTrackingConfig = {}` → experiment with `track()` → `gtag('config', ...)`. With consent denied, gtag.js sends cookieless pings that still include `ep.{customDim}` (and the `trackUser()` property); after the visitor accepts on the page, later events include it too, so don't call `track()` or `gtag('config')` again. Consent Mode only controls Google tags, not the `persist()` cookie/storage or other tools. GA4 reports mainly show visitors who accepted, so a variant that changes the cookie banner (or the content around it) makes the GA4 samples of the variants not comparable. Example: [consent-mode.html](https://github.com/osvik/abrantes/blob/main/examples/consent-mode.html); details in the "Google Consent Mode V2" section of SKILL.md
- Test each variant with `?abrantes_force=MyTest:N` instead of editing the code; check tracking without the parameter, since forced visits aren't tracked
- Debug mode: `?abrantes_debug` in the URL (or `Abrantes.debug = true` before the experiment) logs every step to the console as `Abrantes debug: ...` (assignment, render, persist, tracking, form field value)
- Several experiments on the same page: each needs its own GA4 custom dimension name (e.g. `MyTestA.track("ab_test_a")`, `MyTestB.track("ab_test_b")`), registered in GA4 admin. `settings` is shared by all experiments, so only one experiment per page can use `formTrack()`
- For redirect experiments, add `<link rel="canonical">` on variant pages
- For iframe experiments, verify `event.origin` in postMessage listeners
